title: Global Error Handler
diagramContent:
graph TD
  Route1[Route A fails] -->|next(err)| Global[Global Error Handler]
  Route2[Route B fails] -->|next(err)| Global
  DB[DB Error] -->|next(err)| Global
  Global -->|Log to File| Console
  Global -->|Consistent JSON| Client[Client Browser]
definition: A Global Error Handler is a single `app.use((err, req, res, next))` middleware placed at the end of `server.js` that centralizes all API error responses into one consistent JSON format. It intercepts all `next(err)` calls from anywhere in the application.

answers.question: Define Global Error Handler in your own words.
answers.answer: A Global Error Handler is a single `app.use((err, req, res, next))` middleware placed at the end of `server.js` that centralizes all API error responses into one consistent JSON format.

answers.question: When should you avoid using Global Error Handler?
answers.answer: It depends on the specific architectural requirements and performance bottlenecks of your application. Overusing it can sometimes lead to tightly coupled code.
